synthesis: DEV-2414 made the ClickHouse matcher elect exactly one address per (address geo, hour_bucket, is_staged side) -- verified: ScoutCheckInMatchQuery.php:212 partitions ROW_NUMBER() by (addr_lng, addr_lat, hour_bucket, out_is_staged). But the PostgreSQL storage layer never caught up: platform.scout_check_ins is still keyed unique(kit_id, address_id, hour_bucket) (2026_08_10_170314_create_scout_check_ins_table.php:27) -- an address-shaped key for a place-shaped fact, with is_staged absent from it entirely. Because clarity.scout_open_addresses is rebuilt in place every 15 minutes and the recorder re-matches the same GPS window ~3x on its 5-min cadence / 15-min lookback, the elected winner for a place can change address_id mid-hour without the underlying visit changing. insertOrIgnore then sees a brand-new key and writes a second row for one physical visit. The fix is to make the storage key agree with the election's own partition key, using the addr_lng/addr_lat the query already computes (lines 171-172) but drops before its final SELECT (lines 218-224). Two findings from this reconcile sharpen the ticket materially. (1) Dropping the OLD unique index is mandatory, not optional: because is_staged is not in it, a corrected Direct-side row for an address that moved buckets collides on (kit, address_id, hour) and is silently dropped by insertOrIgnore -- that IS the ticket's 'keeps is_staged = true forever'. With the old index dropped and the geo key in place, no row carries a wrong is_staged any more, which dissolves most of the candidates' dispute about whether a reconciliation UPDATE/DELETE step is needed. (2) What survives is not a bug but an unresolved product decision: mechanism 3 ends with the place legitimately carrying BOTH a Staging and a Direct row, so AC4's per-side reading yields two rows while AC1's literal 'exactly one row for that place in that hour' yields one. That fork changes the unique index itself (whether is_staged is in the key) and cannot be resolved from code -- it is the gating question for a human. Production measurement is in hand: 33.3% of (geo, side) election groups are flip-capable, Open-order churn runs at ~1.0M updates/24h fleet-wide, and simultaneous dual-listing does NOT occur (0 of 4,519,947 address_ids carry both is_staged values), so mechanism 3 is a TEMPORAL label change across book rebuilds.

scope.summary: Thread the elected BOOK address's own coordinate out of ScoutCheckInMatchQuery (it is computed in the addresses/address_hour/ranked CTEs and partitioned on, but never projected), persist it as two new nullable `double precision` columns addr_lng/addr_lat on platform.scout_check_ins, DROP the old unique(kit_id, address_id, hour_bucket), and ADD unique(kit_id, addr_lng, addr_lat, hour_bucket, is_staged) so the storage grain equals the election grain. The new columns are distinct from the existing lat/lng, which are the GPS-FIX coordinate and stay unchanged. No backfill: legacy rows keep NULL geo and PostgreSQL's NULLS DISTINCT default exempts them from the new unique index. insertOrIgnore stays the persistence mechanism. Build must not start before that is answered.

questions.q: MECHANISM-3 GRAIN, the gating decision: when a place's label moves between book rebuilds mid-hour (address 8000 leaves the Staging side and re-appears on the Direct side at the same geo), should that hour hold ONE row for the place or TWO (one per is_staged side)? AC1 says re-running 'produces exactly one row for that place in that hour'; AC4 says N co-located addresses 'still yield one row per is_staged side'. These agree everywhere EXCEPT here. OPTION A (two rows -- is_staged stays in the unique key, pure insertOrIgnore, no UPDATE/DELETE): satisfies AC4 literally, preserves DEV-2414's deliberate both-sides grain and its parity test test_colocated_direct_and_staging_each_record_their_own_check_in, needs no reconciliation step and therefore no lookback-vs-hour-bucket scoping rule. Cost: one physical visit yields two check-ins, which works directly against this ticket's own ~1.0-per-kit target; and note a consequence no candidate spelled out -- both rows would carry address_id 8000, so the DEV-1756-derived per-address consumer pattern COUNT(*) WHERE address_id = ? (backed by the retained index(org_id, address_id)) would count 2 check-ins for one address at one place in one hour, which was impossible under the old index. OPTION B (one row -- drop is_staged from the unique key and relabel the surviving row): satisfies AC1 literally and the ~1.0 target. Cost: regresses DEV-2414's both-sides behaviour, breaks the parity test above, contradicts AC4, requires an UPDATE path (which must hand-stamp updated_at since insertOrIgnore bypasses model events) plus exactly the scoping rule the ticket warns about, and violates okf/concepts/check-in.md's 'immutable event -- first sighting wins'. This decides the shape of the unique index itself, so it must be answered BEFORE build.
questions.answer: TWO rows, one per is_staged side. `is_staged` stays in the uniqueness key; pure insertOrIgnore is retained. This preserves DEV-2414's deliberate both-sides grain and its parity test test_colocated_direct_and_staging_each_record_their_own_check_in, and keeps a co-located Staging order from reading as never-visited. Accepted cost: in the mechanism-3 case one physical visit yields two check-ins, which works against the ~1.0/kit target — judged small because 0 of 4,519,947 book address_ids are currently dual-listed. AC1 is therefore read as per-side (AC4 defines the grain), NOT as a literal one-row-per-place-per-hour cap.
questions.note: This is the crystallised form of the candidates' disagreement about whether an UPDATE/DELETE reconciliation step is needed (1: required; A: purely additive; B: a second row is legitimate per AC4; C: insertOrIgnore suffices, and named the fork). Tracing candidate A's mandatory-index-drop finding dissolves the reconciliation half -- the stranded stale is_staged is caused by the OLD index omitting is_staged, and dropping it fixes that without any UPDATE. What is left is not a mechanism dispute but this product decision. Exposure is measured and non-trivial: mechanism 3 is temporal (0 simultaneous dual-listings in 4.5M book rows) and 33.3% of (geo, side) groups are flip-capable.

Recorded as a known boundary rather than engineered around, because that consumer does not exist yet (okf: "None yet by design") and ->upsert( has no precedent anywhere in app/.

Nothing else needs it: repo-wide grep for scout_check_ins / ScoutCheckIn:: finds only the writer, the model, the migration and the test files -- zero readers exist today (DEV-1756/1757/1758/2258 consumers are unbuilt), and the documented future COUNT(*) WHERE address_id = ? pattern is already served by the untouched index(org_id, address_id).

questions.q: What is the geo key's physical shape -- raw doubles, a rounded/encoded key, a geohash, or a PostGIS point?
questions.answer: Two new nullable `double precision` columns (addr_lng, addr_lat), mirroring the election's own exact-tuple partition and the SQL's own internal CTE aliases (ScoutCheckInMatchQuery.php:171-172). Geohash REJECTED: this repo's existing precedent is intentionally-fuzzy map bucketing at ~19-38m (HitDirectHotspotQuery::DEDUP_PRECISION=8, App\Support\Scout\Geohash), far too coarse -- it would silently collapse addresses the election treats as distinct (test_near_but_not_identical_coordinates_do_not_collapse, ~1m apart) -- and at a precision fine enough to preserve that (~11-12) it adds cell-boundary jitter risk for no benefit. PostGIS point REJECTED: the `=` operator on geometry compares bounding boxes, not exact coordinates, so a plain UNIQUE btree would not mean what it appears to mean (exact equality needs ST_Equals via an exclusion constraint). Float round-trip is safe: ClickHouse FORMAT JSON round-trips Float64 exactly (measured -97.70001 decoding back distinct from -97.7), and while PHP's float-to-string under this environment's precision=14 is NOT bit-exact at ~17 significant digits, the truncation is DETERMINISTIC (the same CH double always yields the same stored PG double, so a later re-election of the same address reproduces the identical key) and 14 significant digits is orders of magnitude finer than the ~1m/5th-decimal-degree distinctness the CH partition relies on.
questions.source: code + empirical (candidate B tinker measurement against the live read-only CH connection, literal constants only; corroborated by candidate A's ClickhouseHttpClient FORMAT JSON + json_decode reading)

questions.q: Should pre-migration rows be backfilled onto the new geo grain, or is the deploy boundary documented?
questions.answer: Document, do not backfill -- mechanically forced, not a style preference. Leaving addr_lng/addr_lat NULL on legacy rows is safe because PostgreSQL's unique-index default is NULLS DISTINCT (NULLS NOT DISTINCT is an explicit PG15+ opt-in this repo does not use), so every legacy row is automatically exempt from the new constraint and can never collide. Backfilling would require deduplicating legacy rows FIRST, because the duplicates this bug already wrote (address 8000 + address 8001 for one visit) are precisely what a new unique(kit_id, addr_lng, addr_lat, hour_bucket, is_staged) index rejects -- the bug's own output would fail the index build. There is also no true source: pre-fix rows only ever stored the GPS-fix coordinate, never the address's own. Matches DEV-2414's own q6 precedent for this same table.

questions.q: How large is platform.scout_check_ins in production, and does the UNIQUE index build need CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY / a maintenance window?
questions.answer: Order 10^3 rows (low thousands), and no -- the index-build lock is a non-issue. The recorder could only ever write in two windows: 2026-08-10 -> 08-12 (DEV-2342's commit records 701 check-ins across 17 cycles, at the pathologically slow 36-148 min pre-DEV-2342 cycle times) and 2026-08-21 08:30 -> 10:10 (~20 cycles at ~2.07 rows/kit over ~44 kits, ~1,800 rows -- the window the DEV-2414 baseline comment 38511 was measured in), plus overlapping ad-hoc manual runs; the schedule is commented out at HEAD (routes/console.php:59-66, commit 4aec6244). Even a generous doubling stays under ~10k. A UNIQUE index build at that size completes in milliseconds, ADD COLUMN nullable-no-default is metadata-only, and CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY is unnecessary (and awkward inside Laravel's transactional migration wrapper anyway). The write path is also QUIESCENT during the migration -- the schedule is off, so there is no concurrent-writer hazard to design around.

questions.q: Must this migration's DDL be hand-applied to production, and in what relation to the code deploy?
questions.answer: Yes -- hand-applied BEFORE the code deploys. This repo has no automated production migration path: app:deploy and the composer post-deploy script list never run migrate (app/Console/Commands/Deploy.php:26-42, composer.json post-deploy), and php artisan migrate itself fails on production because graphqluser lacks CREATE on database zod (ensureAppSchemaExists() throws on a no-op CREATE SCHEMA). Procedure: get the exact SQL via --pretend, run it, insert the migrations row, ALTER ... OWNER TO graphqluser if a different role ran the DDL. If the order is inverted, recordCheckInsForKit() is already inside a per-kit try/catch (ScoutRecordCheckIns.php:113-130, the PG-025 pattern), so a missing-column error degrades to recorded=0 with a per-kit warning rather than crashing -- a safety net, NOT a substitute for correct ordering, because it silently loses every check-in for the misordered window. WHO executes it and WHEN, relative to AC3's before/after runs, remains open (q-open-3).

questions.q: Is insertOrIgnore still a safe persistence mechanism under the recorder's 2-concurrent-slot ceiling with the new key?
questions.answer: Yes, for atomicity. Laravel's insertOrIgnore on pgsql compiles to INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, which Postgres executes atomically per statement against whatever unique index the table carries -- two processes racing on the same (kit_id, addr_lng, addr_lat, hour_bucket, is_staged) tuple have one succeed and one silently no-op, with no deadlock and no extra locking. Moving the key from address_id to geo+is_staged changes only which columns the constraint watches. SCOPED CLAIM: this settles concurrency-safety ONLY. It does not pre-answer whether insertOrIgnore alone produces the RIGHT ROW SET for mechanism 3 -- that is q-open-1.

tests.what_it_pins: MECHANISM 1 (a lower address_id opens at the same geo/side mid-hour). Seed ONE Direct address (id 9001) at geo G plus one in-radius fix; run #1 -> persists (address_id=9001, is_staged=false). Insert a SECOND, LOWER-id Direct address (9000) at the SAME exact geo (book mutation between runs). Run #2 in the same hour with the fix still inside the 15-min lookback. Assert: count === 1 (not 2); the surviving row's address_id is still 9001; matched_at/created_at equal run #1's. This is the assertion the old address_id-keyed index fails, since (kit, 9000, hour) is a brand-new key under the old schema.

MECHANISM 2 ('the frequent one' -- the winner's order closes). Seed TWO co-located Direct addresses at geo G (9000 winner, 9001 loser) plus one in-radius fix; run #1 -> persists address_id=9000. DELETE 9000's row from the book between runs (simulating the rebuild dropping a closed order). Run #2 -> the matcher now elects 9001. Assert: count === 1 (not 2); the surviving row's address_id is STILL 9000 (frozen even though 9000 has left the book entirely); matched_at unchanged.

MECHANISM 3 (the sharp case -- fixture shape and expected row count BOTH depend on q-open-1, so do not write this test until that is answered). Production-faithful setup: seed TWO co-located Staging addresses at geo G (8000 winner, 8001 loser) on an approved staging partner's hotlist plus one in-radius fix; run #1 -> persists (8000, is_staged=true). Between runs DELETE 8000's Staging book row and INSERT 8000 fresh onto a NEW Direct hotlist at the SAME geo -- a temporal move, per flip-risk-measurement.md's zero-dual-listing finding, NOT a simultaneous dual-hotlist listing. Run #2. Under OPTION A the required assertion COMBINATION is: (1) count === 2 -- not 1 (Direct silently dropped, today's bug) and not 3 (a spurious extra Staging row for 8001); (2) exactly 1 row with is_staged=false (the previously-lost Direct visit now lands); (3) exactly 1 row with is_staged=true (no second Staging row); (4) the is_staged=true row's matched_at/created_at equal run #1's exactly (same row, immutable, not rewritten). A count-only check or a new-row-label-only check would each individually pass a broken 'adds a correct row, leaves a stale one behind' implementation -- all four assertions are needed together.

GEO PROVENANCE: the new columns come from the BOOK address, not the GPS fix. Seed a book address at (-97.700000, 30.300000) and a fix at a different in-radius point (e.g. -97.7003, 30.3003, ~35m away, inside the 160.934m radius). Assert the persisted addr_lng/addr_lat equal the BOOK coordinate exactly while lat/lng equal the FIX coordinate. Catches a 'reuse lat/lng as the new key' mistake, which would not be idempotent across cycles at all -- each re-match picks a fresh earliest fix from the sliding window.

POSTGRES-LAYER PRECISION GUARD (the residual on the raw-double key): two book addresses ~1m apart at the same hour/side must persist as TWO distinct rows, mirroring the query-layer test_near_but_not_identical_coordinates_do_not_collapse but asserted through the actual PDO bind + unique index. This is the test that would catch the precision=14 float-stringification truncation silently merging geos ClickHouse treats as distinct.
AC4 REGRESSION: N co-located Direct addresses AND N co-located Staging addresses at the identical geo -> exactly 2 persisted rows, one per side, unchanged by moving the unique key onto the geo pair.

DB-CONSTRAINT DIRECTNESS (only candidate 1 proposed this -- kept): the new unique index itself rejects a duplicate (kit, addr_lng, addr_lat, hour_bucket, is_staged) insert at the database level, not merely via insertOrIgnore's application-level intent. AC1's guarantee is only as strong as the index.

handle()'s return array carries addr_lng/addr_lat equal to the seeded BOOK coordinate and distinct from the fix's lat/lng when the two differ -- a narrower, faster-to-diagnose pin of the plumbing than the end-to-end command tests.

plan_sketch.intent: Run scout:record-check-ins twice in one UTC hour with a book mutation between runs, once per flip mechanism (a lower address_id opens at the same geo; the elected winner's order closes and a higher id takes over). Assert exactly one platform.scout_check_ins row per (kit, geo, hour, side), and that the surviving row's address_id/matched_at/created_at are unchanged from run #1 (proving preservation, not replacement).

Cover all three mechanisms. For mechanism 3 use the production-faithful TEMPORAL fixture (DELETE the Staging book row, INSERT the same address_id onto a Direct hotlist at the same geo between runs) -- never a simultaneous dual-hotlist listing, which does not occur in production. Assert the full four-part combination (total count, exactly one row per side, and the original row's timestamps unchanged); a count-only or label-only check passes a broken implementation. EXPECTED ROW COUNT DEPENDS ON q-open-1 -- do not author this scenario until that is answered.

Geo provenance: assert the persisted addr_lng/addr_lat equal the BOOK address coordinate while lat/lng equal the GPS-FIX coordinate (seed them at different in-radius points, ~35m apart). Plus a Postgres-layer precision guard: two book addresses ~1m apart at the same hour/side must persist as two distinct rows.

Operator with production access runs scout:record-check-ins manually BEFORE the change (the 'before' recorded/kits_processed from the completion log line, comparable to DEV-2414's 2.07/kit baseline in comment 38511), then AFTER the DDL is hand-applied and the code deployed. Sequence matters: before-run, DDL, deploy, after-run. Not automatable -- the schedule is disabled and the book is live production data.

Seed N co-located Direct AND N co-located Staging addresses at one identical geo; assert exactly 2 persisted rows, one per side. Also re-run the existing DEV-2414 co-located and multi-distinct-geo tests unmodified and confirm they stay green with the new schema in place.

qa_hint.seed_scenario: One org with a Scout-enabled kit (valid kit_mapping, kit_settings row, clarity-scout permission) and a driver. Seed clarity.scout_open_addresses with 2-3 co-located address_ids at ONE exact coordinate -- mixing Direct and Staging across the three mechanism scenarios -- plus one genuinely distant address and one ~1m-away address as no-collapse controls. Seed one or two clarity.sc_positions fixes inside the 160.934m radius, timed within a single UTC hour so hour_bucket stays fixed across both recorder invocations, and anchored near now() via travelTo() for determinism (NOT for TTL survival -- neither CH table carries a TTL). Run the recorder, MUTATE THE BOOK, run it again in the same hour, then inspect platform.scout_check_ins row count and the persisted is_staged / address_id / addr_lng / addr_lat / matched_at values. The book mutation between runs is the whole point: no existing test does it, so it is where all three mechanisms live.

disagreements.topic: Does the bucket-migration case (mechanism 3) need an UPDATE/DELETE reconciliation step, or does pure insertOrIgnore on the new key suffice?
disagreements.positions: 1: reconciliation REQUIRED (the old bucket goes empty and stops being emitted, so nothing re-collides with the stale row). A: purely additive, no DELETE/UPDATE, and the scoping question therefore never arises. B: a second row on the new side is legitimate per AC4. C: insertOrIgnore suffices, and explicitly named the fork rather than resolving it.
disagreements.resolution: PARTLY RESOLVED FROM CODE, THEN ESCALATED. Candidate A's mandatory-index-drop finding, traced against the actual index (migration :27, is_staged absent), shows the stranding is caused by the OLD index dropping the corrected Direct row -- so with it dropped, no row carries a wrong is_staged and no reconciliation mechanism is needed for that symptom. Candidate 1's premise was therefore inverted, not merely outvoted. What survives is NOT a mechanism dispute but a product decision -- whether one physical visit at a re-labelled place should yield one row or two -- which is recorded as q-open-1 with both options and their consequences, answered:false. Not picked.

disagreements.topic: Attribution staleness: should address_id/hotlist_id be refreshed to the current winner, or frozen at first sighting?
disagreements.positions: All four raised it; none resolved it. A and C each explicitly declined to settle it unilaterally despite okf/concepts/check-in.md:24 leaning toward freezing.
disagreements.resolution: Carried forward as q-open-2, answered:false. Unanimously unresolved is not the same as settled, and it changes what is persisted.

disagreements.topic: Is the raw-double geo key safe across the CH-Float64 -> JSON -> PHP-float -> PG-double round trip?
disagreements.positions: A: answered yes from code (passthrough value, no arithmetic; the existing lat/lng already round-trip through the same client). B: answered yes EMPIRICALLY -- CH FORMAT JSON round-trips exactly, and PHP's precision=14 stringification is not bit-exact at ~17 significant digits but is deterministic and far finer than the ~1m grain the partition relies on. 1 and C: left it open (2-2 split); C leaned the same way as A and B but flagged the round trip as a genuine unmeasured risk.
disagreements.resolution: RESOLVED ON B'S MEASUREMENT (grounded beats confident): C's uncertainty was about a FACT, and B measured that fact -- the ideal case for resolving from ground truth rather than escalating. Recorded answered:true with the measurement and the rejection rationale for geohash/PostGIS. C's concern was NOT dropped: it is carried as a mandatory test obligation (a Postgres-layer near-but-not-identical assertion, the exact failure mode that would silently defeat the index) plus a note. Flagged here because the split was 2-2 and this is the one place the merge overrode two candidates' 'needs-human'.
disagreements.gate_effect: non-blocking (gate is already BLOCKED on other grounds, so this resolution did not change the outcome)

disagreements.topic: Production row count of platform.scout_check_ins and whether the UNIQUE index build needs CONCURRENTLY or a maintenance window.
disagreements.positions: All four left it UNRESOLVED with a non-empty resource_envelope.unresolved (1/B/C recorded oracle_status unavailable, A recorded not-configured). Anchors offered ranged from '818 rows' to 'low hundreds to low thousands' to 'unknown'.
disagreements.resolution: SETTLED by driver evidence that post-dated every candidate: the recorder could only write in two narrow windows (701 rows / 17 cycles, then ~1,800 rows), bounding the table at order 10^3, which makes the index build a milliseconds operation with a quiescent write path. oracle_status corrected to `ok` with an explicit table-not-in-oracle note -- the CDC oracle works (zod.public_address = 198,128,783); it simply never mirrored this platform-schema table. `unresolved` emptied, so the envelope does not gate the run on a probe failure that did not happen.
disagreements.gate_effect: non-blocking (was the fourth reason all four candidates escalated; now closed)

disagreements.topic: Mechanism 3's physical mechanism: simultaneous dual-listing via min(is_staged), or a temporal label change?
disagreements.positions: Candidates 1, A and C all described it the ticket's way (an address that ALSO joins a Direct hotlist, collapsed by min(is_staged)). B alone folded in the driver's measurement contradicting that.
disagreements.resolution: SETTLED by measurement, overriding three candidates and the ticket's own wording and the class docblock: 0 of 4,519,947 address_ids carry both is_staged values, so simultaneous dual-listing does not occur in production. Mechanism 3 is a TEMPORAL label change across book rebuilds. This changes the required test fixture (DELETE + re-INSERT on the other side, not a dual-hotlist listing) and is recorded in notes, ACs and tests. Corollary: the argMin Direct-wins tiebreak and the parity tests pinning it guard a book state with zero production instances.
disagreements.gate_effect: non-blocking (changes HOW to build and test, not WHETHER)

reconcile.method_note: Applied insightlpr:multi-candidate-merge. Additive content unioned and deduped by file+intent (6 core files -> 10 with the backstop; 3 test scenarios -> 13 test obligations). Agreements verified against the repo rather than accepted on consensus -- the mandatory-index-drop claim, the CTE line numbers, the schedule state and all cited test method names were each read directly, and every citation in this artifact was confirmed to exist. Disagreements were resolved from ground truth where ground truth existed (index drop, geo-key shape, row-count bound, mechanism 3's physical form) and escalated where it did not (the AC1/AC4 fork, attribution staleness, AC3 ownership). Confidence 80 is set ABOVE the best single candidate (78) because the union closed four items that every candidate had left open -- including the resource envelope that all four flagged -- and BELOW 85 because q-open-1 can still change the unique index itself, which is the deliverable's load-bearing decision.
